text:
jamie: Heads-up — after last night's GPU firmware roll (eu-west-1), we're seeing per-token latency drift on shared pools.
jamie: spike started ~03:10 UTC, affects p4 and a100 slices. not a total outage but P95 up ~220ms -> 520ms for some tenants.
jamie: adding logs: `rpc_performance: avg=85ms p95=520ms driver_version=2.14.7` — not seen on eu-central.
sanjay: ack. any correlation with NIC/driver combos? last change was kernel bump + firmware.
kira: checked kernel logs, a few WARN lines around NVLINK init, plus `nvidia-smi -q` shows inconsistent PSTATE on some nodes.
maria: @jamie can you tag which pools? want to decide routing fallback and whether to cordon nodes.
jamie: affected pools: shared-gpu-eu-west-shared-1, shared-gpu-eu-west-shared-3. Dedicated pools unaffected.
infra-bot: deploybot: firmware-rollout eu-west-1 completed on 2026-03-17T02:45:00Z (batch size 60 nodes)
sanjay: suggestion: temporarily prefer dedicated pools for high-SLO tenants and route best-effort to patched shared pools. we should throttle batch autoscaler to avoid pushing more workloads onto impacted racks.
kira: +1. also propose enabling per-tenant isolation weights so heavy KV cache users don't push tokens into slow paths.
maria: cost callout — moving tenants to dedicated short-term will increase spend ~25% for those customers, need gating from product if >$5k/day.
jamie: ops plan: 1) roll back firmware on a subset to confirm it's root cause (will do on 4 nodes), 2) enable routing fallback to dedicated for flagged tenants, 3) increase telemetry sampling on P95 and nvlink errors.
jamie: rollback command I'm running: ```ansible-playbook -i eu-west hosts/firmware_rollback.yml --limit 'hwpool:shared-eu-west' -e target_version=2.14.5``` 
kira: keep a watch on PCIe/RTCore logs, I suspect a scheduling regression with 2.14.7.
sanjay: if rollback proves it, we should pause rollout and re-evaluate kernel pairing. also open a vendor ticket with full logs — include `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` and `journalctl -u gpu-driver --since "2026-03-17 02:00"` dump.
jamie: rollback started on node eu-w-34 at 03:40 UTC.
infra-bot: monitor: alert suppressed for shared-gpu-eu-west-shared-1 for 30m per jamie request.
maria: pinging product on cost tradeoffs and which tenants to failover. assigning to @product-lead.
product-lead: (in thread) thanks — recommend we target high-SLA tenants (enterprise) for immediate dedicated fallback. will contact affected customers.
kira: quick mitigation: add small eBPF qdisc to limit kv-cache egress bursts on shared pools, reduces tail latency for others. can push at 04:00 if ops approves.
sanjay: record decision: if rollback reduces P95 by >150ms, resume rollout after vendor patch. else keep rollout paused and escalate.
jamie: update: after rollback on eu-w-34, P95 dropped from 520ms -> 190ms for that node's slice. looks like firmware is the culprit.
product-lead: got confirmation from two customers impacted; they're ok with temporary dedicated failover while we stabilize.
maria: thanks. I'll open a short-lived dedicated reservation for up to 72 hours and track cost delta.
jamie: follow-ups: vendor ticket opened #VT-8932, adding logs and the rollback experiment notes. will post final remediation plan once vendor replies.
sanjay: good work. let's schedule a postmortem tomorrow 09:30 UTC to decide rollout gating and release criteria.
jamie: closing loop here — will update channel after vendor response. :thumbsup:
